key_insight: UNSM changes the local hardness of Cr3C2–NiCr coatings in a strongly sample- and process-dependent way, with detonation-sprayed coatings showing a narrower hardness range than HVOF coatings.
engineering_relevance: For wear-resistant thermal-spray coatings, post-treatment can improve or redistribute near-surface mechanical properties, but the response must be verified locally rather than assumed from the coating route alone.
method: Compared detonation-sprayed (DS) and HVOF Cr3C2–NiCr coatings after ultrasonic nanocrystal surface modification (UNSM).
Tested four treated samples per deposition route at 20/30 N static load and 20/30 µm vibration amplitude.
Measured instrumental hardness at 300 mN load and examined post-scratch SEM morphology.
evidence_signal: Hardness values ranged from 820–970 HV for DS and 546–1165 HV for HVOF, with the highest values at DS-T1 (20 N/20 µm) and HVOF-T4 (30 N/30 µm); scratch SEM showed heterogeneous contrast and crack-like features.
watch_item: The SEM observations are qualitative and do not isolate damage caused specifically by UNSM, so scratch resistance ranking should not be inferred directly.
paper_title: HARDNESS AND POST-SCRATCH SURFACE MORPHOLOGY OF Cr₃C₂–NiCr COATINGS AFTER ULTRASONIC NANOCRYSTAL SURFACE MODIFICATION
